questions: Do you have involuntary movements of your arms or hands outside of these examinations?
Do these movements consist mainly of sudden, brief jerks rather than continuous shaking?
Are the movements triggered or worsened when you voluntarily move, reach, or start walking?
Can you temporarily suppress the movements if you concentrate?
Do you feel an uncomfortable urge or mounting inner tension before the movement?
Do the movements disappear completely when you are asleep?
Do they occur in sudden attacks with normal movement between attacks?
Does startle, stress, excitement, or lack of sleep bring on or worsen the attacks?
Do you remain fully conscious and aware during the episodes?
Have you ever lost consciousness, bitten your tongue, or lost bladder control during one?
Do the movements affect your legs, trunk, face, or voice as well as your arms?
Did these movements begin before you started taking zonisamide?
Did stopping zonisamide clearly worsen the movements?
Did restarting zonisamide clearly improve them within a few weeks?
Have you ever had a similar movement disorder before, or does anyone in your family have similar symptoms?
Are you taking any medications that block dopamine, such as antipsychotics or metoclopramide?
Do you have stiffness, slowness, balance problems, or reduced arm swing when walking?
Do you have numbness, weakness, or loss of coordination in either arm?
